conviction_note: Seven small, mostly offsetting findings sum to +0.5. The name's median reaction is 2.14% with no usable option chain, so abs_move is set at 2.8 because hunter sizes have run too small. p_up is 55: the bar ($0.63) sits under the Q2 adjusted run-rate ($0.64), the September Fed hike helps a bank whose own ALCO model is asset-sensitive, and 5 of 7 prior prints rose. Nothing decisive and unpriced was found. The scaled +0.28 and the findings sum +0.5 agree in sign.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus $0.63, revenue ~$293-294m. Three sources agree: Benzinga forecast table (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HOMB/earnings-forecasts), Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/HOMB, rev $292.7m) and AlphaQuery (https://www.alphaquery.com/stock/HOMB/earnings-history). Q2 2026 printed adjusted $0.64 against a $0.62 consensus (8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001331520/000133152026000106/homb063026earningsrelease.htm). The company gives no quantitative EPS guide; on the Q2 call management said it will no longer forecast next-quarter loan growth.
positioning_check: Short interest 9,907,152 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, ~5.0% of 200.05m shares, 5.98 days to cover. That is flat against 9.95m on 09-15 and up from 8.53m on 08-31 (https://equibles.com/stocks/homb/short-interest, read 2026-10-14), so the short is not crowded. No skew: the 2026-10-16 option chain is empty in the baseline. Tape: spot $28.33, -4.74% over 20 days, -10.0% from the 52-week high. Mid-August quotes were around $30.4-31.6 (Robinhood 2026-08-19 $30.41), so the stock has given up ~7-10% since the Q2 print with no company-specific cause found.

findings.finding: The Fed raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, its first hike since 2023. On the Q2 call (2026-07-15) HOMB said its ALCO model shows nearly +6% net interest income for a +100bp shock and that a modest hike would be a net positive. Pro rata the hike is about +1.5% NII, roughly +$4m a quarter or ~+$0.015 EPS, landing almost entirely in Q4, so it surfaces as NIM commentary on the 2026-10-15 call rather than in the Q3 number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HOMB trades on NIM stability and the margin narrative. Q2 2026 (NIM flat at 4.51%, record revenue, adj EPS beat) rose +4.78%. Q1 2026, with the margin flagged to tick down on MCB, fell -3.36%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were paying for an asset-sensitive bank getting a hike, HOMB would have held or outperformed since 09-16. It is instead -4.7% over 20 days and ~10% off its August level. Consensus at $0.63 sits below the Q2 adjusted $0.64, which does not look like a bar that embeds NII upside. Offsetting this: the deposit-cost reaction to the hike (about $1.25bn of 2H26 CDs repricing at mid-3%) is unknown and is the main risk to the sign.
findings.independence: The company sensitivity comes from a machine-generated Q2 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-15-home-bancshares-inc-conway-ar-stock/, 2026-07-15), not the 10-Q rate-shock table, which could not be read. Peer read in the same direction: Regions guided 3Q26 NIM stable to modestly higher (finding 6).

findings.finding: Q3 loan balances face elevated payoffs. On the Q2 call management said Q3 payoffs 'could be there' at the Q2 level of just over $1bn, that 'we have work to do in order to post loan growth in this quarter', and that it would stop forecasting next-quarter loan growth. Against that, ~$350m of mostly South Florida loans had just been approved. In Q2, legacy loans rose +$26m against an internal forecast of a ~$600m decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat its own loan-decline forecast and the stock rose +4.78%. Q3 2025 had a CCFG organic loan decline of -$59.4m and the stock fell -3.39%, but that was the October 2025 regional-bank credit scare.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: management told the market to expect flat-to-down legacy loans. This sits inside what the company guided, so it is sized near zero. The residual is whether the ~$350m of approvals funded in Q3. That cannot be seen until the release.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/16/home-bancshares-homb-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/) also projected 'very high' Q2 and Q3 payoffs approaching $1bn each. It is the same company source, so this is one finding.

findings.finding: The buyback slowed after Q2. Shares outstanding were 200.46m at 2026-06-30 and 200,049,630 at 2026-08-06 (10-Q cover), about 0.41m net retired in five weeks, against 1.5m ($40.5m) in Q2. Management said it was about halfway to buying back the ~5.5m Mountain Commerce shares, with ~15m shares authorised and ~$450m of parent cash. The stock then fell to ~$28-29, where a 'extremely aggressive' buyer would step up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction specific to this line. Buybacks run steadily at about 0.5-1.5m shares a quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Share count is a sub-1% EPS item and nobody prices it ahead of the release. Whether Q3 repurchases accelerated on the dip is unknown.
findings.independence: The 1.5m shares in Q2 and the 'halfway' remark come from the Q2 8-K and the call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-15-home-bancshares-inc-conway-ar-stock/).

findings.finding: Two open-market insider sales followed the Q2 print. Centennial Bank CEO John Stephen Tipton sold 12,000 shares at $31.59 on 2026-08-04, and director Jim Rankin sold 15,000 at $30.86 on 2026-08-11. Both were near the 52-week high, about 10% above today's spot, and there were no insider buys.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None observed. Smaller routine insider sales on 2026-04-21 and 2026-06-01 preceded the +4.78% Q2 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Small sales (~$0.84m in total) that the market ignores. They carry information only because one seller runs the bank, and they predate the drawdown. Holdings retained are large, so read them as diversification more than signal.
findings.independence: Tipton's Form 4 (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/HOMB/form-4-home-bancshares-inc-insider-trading-activity-83b603be8cc3.html, filed 2026-08-05) is a separate filing.

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 (105 mph) near Destin, Florida on 2026-10-09, damaging Pensacola and cutting power to 440-664k customers in the Florida Panhandle and South Alabama. Centennial Bank has a large Panhandle franchise: 29 Panhandle branches before it took Doral's Panama City/Pensacola branches in 2015, and a Destin office. The storm is after quarter-end, so it is not in Q3 numbers, but management will be asked about it on the call. In 2017 Hurricane Irma cost HOMB a $33.4m storm accrual in the quarter it hit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2017: profits fell 66% on Irma-related expenses (https://talkbusiness.net/2017/10/home-bancshares-3q-profits-fall-66-on-hurricane-irma-related-expenses/). The stock reaction then is not in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The 5-day run-up is +0.53%, so the stock shows no reaction to the storm. A Cat 2 Panhandle hit is far smaller than Irma, so the likely outcome is a 'minimal impact' remark or a small Q4 reserve commentary. Sized small because this is weather-to-company inference.
findings.independence: The branch footprint comes from a separate source (https://talkbusiness.net/2015/02/home-bancshares-taking-over-another-bank-in-florida-panhandle/, 2015) and is old. The current Panhandle loan concentration is not verified.

findings.finding: Peers that spoke after HOMB's Q2 call point to a benign Q3 margin backdrop. Regions' Aug-Sep 2026 investor deck guided 3Q26 NII up ~2% and NIM stable to modestly higher against 2Q26's 3.66%. Wells Fargo reported a Q3 2026 NIM of 2.43%, flat quarter on quarter, and guided Q4 stable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measured for HOMB on peer reads. HOMB's own NIM of 4.51% is far above both peers and driven by its own loan yields.
findings.why_not_priced: This is industry context, largely in every bank model already. It is a proxy for HOMB, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Wells Fargo Q3 2026 release (https://www.wellsfargo.com/assets/pdf/about/investor-relations/earnings/third-quarter-2026-earnings.pdf, 2026-10-14) is a different company and document.

findings.finding: The Q3 bar of $0.63 sits below Q2's adjusted $0.64, though Mountain Commerce was already a full-quarter contributor in Q2 (closed 2026-04-01). Q3 adds expense discipline (management targets ~$120m a quarter against Q2's $122.7m ex-merger), flat-to-better charge-offs (Q2 $5.8m), and accretion from early payoffs that 'may recur'. HOMB beat in each of the last two quoted quarters: Q2 2026 $0.64 vs $0.62, and Q3 2025 $0.63 vs $0.60.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats: Q2 2026 +4.78%, Q3 2025 -3.39% (beat sold during the sector credit scare), Jan 2026 +0.91%. On this line 5 of 7 prior reactions were up and the median absolute move was 2.14%.
findings.why_not_priced: A consensus a cent under the prior adjusted quarter on a bank with a stable 4.5% NIM leaves room for a small beat. Against that, beats have been only partly paid (Q3 2025 was sold). Sized small because it is inference from run-rate, not an unseen number.
findings.independence: The consensus figures come from Benzinga, Earnings Whispers and AlphaQuery, which are independent of the 8-K run-rate. The expense and charge-off guidance comes from the call summary that findings 1-2 share (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-15-home-bancshares-inc-conway-ar-stock/).

outside_window.finding: Mountain Commerce system conversion is scheduled for November 2026, and ~$5.5m/yr of cost saves land mostly from mid-Q4. This shows up in Q4 and 2027 numbers, not in this print, beyond call commentary.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR filing list since 2026-07-01: only the 07-15 8-K, the 10-Q (08-07), a 13G (07-31), two Form 144s and three Form 4s. No 8-K for a buyback change, credit event, M&A or executive change (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001331520).
Analyst actions September-October 2026: none found. The latest are Cantor raising its target to $31 on 2026-08-19 and July target raises; average target ~$33.
Company-specific news explaining the ~10% drawdown since August: none found.

Centennial/CCFG litigation or large credit events: only a $42k Saline County foreclosure (Tim's Tavern) and a Texas Chapter 7 adversary scheduling entry, both immaterial. Nothing on the ~$100m largest nonperforming credit.
Southern regional peers reporting before 10-14 (Hancock Whitney reports 10-20): none had printed.
Q3 FFIEC call report: not yet filed (due late October).
10-Q rate-shock table and monthly repurchase table: the fetch truncated, so neither could be read.

rejected_candidates.detail: The article is dated 2026-07-08 and previews Q2, not Q3. Its date contradicts its use as the Q3 bar.
The company's own 2026-09-14 announcement sets the release for 10-14 after the close.
Immaterial ordinary-course workout. It is covered by the general credit line in finding 7 (charge-offs guided flat to better), so it is not filed separately.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with, since the chain is empty. The small positive lean cuts against the -4.7% 20-day run-up and the ~10% slide from August. That slide has no company cause found, so it could equally be priced caution, and that keeps p_up at 55 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxy and macro-to-company transmission sized small): hurricane cut from -0.3 to -0.2, Regions/WFC peer read from +0.2 to +0.1, Fed-hike finding from +0.6 to +0.5 because the sensitivity figure comes from a machine-generated call summary rather than the 10-Q table.
Lesson 1/6 (the bar-below-run-rate item is inference, and beats have been sold before): cut from +0.4 to +0.3.
Insider sales cut from -0.2 to -0.1? No, left at -0.2: routine and small, already sized for that.
Lesson 6: bar verified against three agreeing estimate sources ($0.63), so no cap applied. The payoff finding lies inside management's own guide and stays near zero.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (5% of float, ~6 days to cover, not crowded), so the negatives were not cut for squeeze risk.
